property: the allowlist suppresses the values it declares and NOTHING ELSE - an undeclared secret at a formerly path-excluded location must still be reported
limits: Establishes that the allowlist is SCOPED - that it hides the declared values and not the paths they happen to live in. It does NOT establish that each declared value is one we were right to allow: the control cannot tell a synthetic fixture token from a real credential someone decided to declare, and nothing can. That judgement is per-entry and lives in the justifications in tests/test_gitleaks_allowlist.py. It also says nothing about which repository paths are scanned - the cases are scanned as their own root, so the repository's path entries cannot apply. That is the coverage probe's property, in .woodpecker.yml.

cases.name: unallowlisted-secret
cases.why: a fabricated AWS key that is NOT in the allowlist, at scripts/secrets-mask.sh - the exact path a whole-file entry excluded until #264. The path is the point: under the old config this was silently suppressed, which is the exposure #264 removed.

cases.name: allowlisted-value
cases.why: the same path carrying AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE, which the allowlist does declare. Separates a correctly scoped allowlist from a scanner wedged at 'report everything'.

anchors.why: the config as it stood the moment before #264, byte-for-byte from `git show 87ddf7d:.gitleaks.toml`. It carries the three whole-file path entries, one of which is `scripts/secrets-mask\.sh` - so it MISSES the unallowlisted secret this control plants there. That is not a hypothetical about what a broad entry could hide: it is the repository's own previous configuration, hiding it, on every run.
